# the contributor audit: block normalization and explicit dense-lattice depth


empty-normal convention.** I read the complete note
`candidate 7cb4b1bb7928127e`.

The maximal inscribed simplex exists and bounds every barycentric
coordinate in absolute value by one. The explicit inscribed ball and
the enclosing radius R=N(N+2) are correct. Rotating the image of the
original vertical subspace to the standard vertical subspace makes the
total invertible map block triangular, so its induced lattice coset and
its common fiber Jacobian are tracked exactly. Formula (4) multiplies
all mixed masses by |det A||det T| and therefore preserves normalized
depth for every transformed halfspace.

The sampled-cap discrepancy is the already independently audited uniform
one and includes both lower-dimensional intersections and sampled
boundary mass. The support-distance integral gives the claimed
R^(-N) interior ball about the ordinary centroid. Rounding only the
base by the covering radius keeps the selected point strictly inside
the body under the stated bound. The ordinary cap slab loss is at most
kappa_(N-1) R^(N-1) delta in every full ambient unit-normal direction.

The decisive estimate is the difference nu(H)-alpha nu(K), so it does
not use an invalid quotient with a potentially negative numerator.
Both delta thresholds make this difference nonnegative. The elementary
variant with no ball-volume constants is more restrictive in the stated
direction. The exact gap holds in every claimed (n,d) case; n=1,d=0
is separately handled by a discrete median. The note now explicitly
excludes n=d=0, consistently with the task's halfspace definition.

For n=1 the transformed spacing is |a| and the transformed projection
length is |a|W<=2R. Hence delta<=R/W, and the displayed width criterion
and n=d=1 example W>=1024 follow. This is a sufficient regime condition,
not a deduction that all bodies have small normalized covering radius.
An originally zero d-volume mixed set cannot satisfy the condition,
because the constructed interior sampled point would give positive
d-dimensional fiber volume. No intrinsic mass is misidentified.
